newsitem.title: UK: Airlines should learn cargo fuel surcharge lesson.
newsitem.headline: Airlines should learn cargo fuel surcharge lesson.

text.p: Last year's heavy criticism of the way airlines introduced fuel surcharges on cargo rates should better equip them to deal with future jet fuel cost rises, a senior Air Canada cargo executive said.
Fuel prices had been rising for some months before surcharges were introduced last October/November, with some carriers giving little notice.

There may have been some opportunism by some airlines in imposing jet fuel price surcharges at a seasonal airfreight peak period, Air Canada general manager cargo for Europe, Africa and Middle East, Des Vertannes, told Reuters in an interview.
"There is no question the (air cargo) market was angered by the very short notice given by carriers," he stated.

Two weeks ago, the UK Air Freight Forum -- made up of carriers, shippers and forwarders -- said it would ask the International Air Transport Association (IATA) to investigate setting up a mechanism to track fuel prices and alert airlines when surcharges might need to be imposed.
Vertannes said if IATA got involved it could only be on timing but "this is a good idea as it would bring discipline".
But IATA could not interfere on the size of surcharges or rate increases as this was a competitive area between carriers quite apart from having anti-trust implications, he added.
The industry agrees higher fuel costs must be recovered but views differ on whether this should be through a surcharge or higher rates.

Shippers preferred it included in a rate which they could try to negotiate lower while forwarders generally preferred a separately billed and transparent surcharge which did not involve them in the same haggling over total freight costs, Vertannes said.
